title: Gaussian limit of cube noise phases
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $a,b\in\mathbb R^n$. For each natural number $m$, average over all pairs $x,y\in\{0,1\}^{nm}$ the noise kernel at parameter $\rho$ times the complex phase whose angle is the sum, over the $n$ blocks, of the corresponding coordinates of $a$ and $b$ paired with the normalized sign sums of $x$ and $y$. After multiplying this average by $2^{-nm}$, the resulting sequence converges as $m\to\infty$ to the expectation of the phase with angle $\sum_{i=1}^n(a_i Z_i+b_i W_i)$, where $(Z,W)$ has the correlated Gaussian measure of parameter $\rho$ on $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n$.
hypotheses_covered: $a,b$ are real-valued functions on the $n$ coordinates
